subject: Modeling large mammal in cold region

messages.author: ad331caa97d1c9b0
messages.subject: Modeling large mammal in cold region
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to model an adult mammoth in a cold environment. But it always returns that "panting/'sweating' options are exhausted". I could fix this if I use "SUBQFAT = 0", but it seems that this does not reflect reality. Any suggestions? Your help would be most appreciated! Here is the code I used:

endoR(
  TA = 4,  ## air temperature at local height (°C)
  TGRD = 4, ## ground temperature (°C)
  TSKY = 4, ## sky temperature (°C)
  TCONDSB = 4, ## surface temperature for conduction (°C)
  TBUSH = 4,
  VEL = 3,  ## wind speed (m/s)
  QSOLR = 600, ## solar radiation, horizontal plane (W/m2)
  Z = 26, ## zenith angle of sun (degrees from overhead)
  AMASS = 6000, #kg
  SHAPE = 1, ## shape, 1 is cylinder, 2 is sphere, 3 is plate, 4 is ellipsoid
  SHAPE_B = 4.7/2.6, ## current ratio between long and short axis (-)  
  FURTHRMK = 0.025, ## user-specified fur thermal conductivity (W/mK), not used if 0
  ZFURD =  40E-3,  ## fur depth, dorsal (m)
  ZFURV = 40E-3,  ## fur depth, ventral (m)
  TC = 35.9,  ## core temperature (°C)  ## Coping with heat: behavioural and physiological responses of savanna elephants in their natural habitat
  TC_MAX = 39, ## maximum core temperature (°C)
  DIFTOL = 0.001,  ## error tolerance for SIMULSOL (°C)
  THERMOREG = 1, ## thermoregulate? (1 = yes, 0 = no)
  RESPIRE = 1, ## respiration? (1 = yes, 0 = no)
  TAREF = 4, ## air temperature at reference height (°C)
  ELEV = 37,  ## elevation (m)
  ABSSB = 0.4,  ## solar absorptivity of substrate (fractional, 0-1)  
  SUBQFAT = 1
)  ##  bush temperature (°C)

All the best,

Liang

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Modeling large mammal in cold region
parts:
Hi Liang,
I've never tried such a large endotherm before but if you change the tolerance for the solution you'll get it to give a result, e.g. DIFTOL = 1.
All the best,
Mike
